terms.definitionEn: A complete instruction that an engine can evaluate.
terms.definitionAr: تعليمة كاملة في الكود يقدر محرك JavaScript ينفذها أو يقيّم نتيجتها.

terms.definitionEn: Text in source code that the JavaScript engine ignores as an instruction.
terms.definitionAr: ملاحظة جوه الكود بتساعد القارئ، والمحرك بيتجاهلها وقت التنفيذ.

terms.definitionEn: A named binding that can refer to a value.
terms.definitionAr: اسم بنربطه بقيمة عشان نقدر نستخدمها أو نغيّرها بعدين.

terms.definitionEn: The creation of a named binding in a program.
terms.definitionAr: خطوة بننشئ فيها اسم جديد ونخليه متاح للاستخدام في البرنامج.

terms.definitionEn: Giving a binding its first value as it is created.
terms.definitionAr: أول قيمة بنحطها للاسم وقت إنشائه.

terms.definitionEn: Storing a value in an existing writable binding.
terms.definitionAr: تخزين قيمة جديدة في اسم موجود ومسموح بتغييره.

terms.definitionEn: A name used to refer to a binding or other program entity.
terms.definitionAr: اسم رمزي بنستخدمه عشان نشاور على متغير أو دالة أو عنصر في الكود.

terms.definitionEn: The rule that treats uppercase and lowercase letters as different characters.
terms.definitionAr: قاعدة بتخلي الحروف الكبيرة والصغيرة مختلفة، فـ name وName مش نفس الاسم.

terms.definitionEn: A declared binding that has not yet been given an explicit value.
terms.definitionAr: اسم اتعمل في الكود ولسه ماخدش قيمة صريحة.

terms.definitionEn: The environment that executes a program and provides its built-in capabilities.
terms.definitionAr: البيئة اللي بتشغّل البرنامج وبتوفر له إمكانيات جاهزة زي console.

terms.definitionEn: An error raised when source text does not follow the language grammar.
terms.definitionAr: خطأ بيظهر لما كتابة الكود ماتتبعش قواعد اللغة.

terms.definitionEn: A named binding that cannot be assigned a different value after creation.
terms.definitionAr: اسم مينفعش نربطه بقيمة تانية بعد إنشائه، حتى لو محتوى object قابل للتغيير.

questions.question: When would you choose let rather than const for a binding?
keyPoints: const prevents reassignment of the binding
Prefer const when reassignment is unnecessary
The choice does not make an object deeply immutable
questions.modelAnswer: Use let when the binding needs to be assigned a new value later, such as a running counter. Prefer const when reassignment is not needed; const protects the binding itself, not the contents of an object it references.

questions.question: What is the difference between an uninitialized binding and one explicitly assigned null?
keyPoints: An uninitialized let binding has value undefined
Both can indicate absence but express different intent
Check the actual value rather than assuming
questions.modelAnswer: A declared let binding without an initializer has the value undefined. Assigning null stores an explicit value, often used to represent intentional absence, so the two values are distinct.

questions.question: What does it mean that JavaScript identifiers are case-sensitive?
keyPoints: Names differing by case can be separate bindings
References must match the declared spelling
A case mismatch can produce an unresolved-name error
questions.modelAnswer: JavaScript distinguishes uppercase and lowercase characters in identifiers, so item and Item are different names. A reference must use the exact spelling of the declaration or it may refer to another binding or fail to resolve.
